assessment.nobel_worthiness: Population-scale administrative evidence transformed the measurement and explanation of intergenerational mobility, with broad influence on research and policy.
assessment.attribution: Chetty and Hendren are central to the empirical and conceptual mobility program; Friedman is a closely associated contributor to its data-intensive implementation.
assessment.maturity: The work has accumulated substantial replication, extension, and influence across more than a decade.
uncertainties: The discovery spans a large collaborative literature, making a three-person allocation necessarily incomplete.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: This work made trade, technology, task change, and local labour-market adjustment empirically central to accounts of wage inequality and employment change.
assessment.attribution: Autor, Dorn, and Hanson form a coherent core for the trade-shock and changing-labour-demand evidence.
assessment.maturity: Its methods, findings, and ensuing debate have been extensively developed and tested over many years.
uncertainties: Separating the effects of trade, technology, and institutions remains empirically challenging.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Correspondence studies supplied unusually direct and persuasive evidence on labour-market discrimination and reshaped empirical practice in the area.
assessment.attribution: Bertrand and Mullainathan's prominent audit-study contribution is readily identifiable within the broader experimental discrimination literature.
assessment.maturity: The design has been widely replicated, adapted, and scrutinized across markets and countries.
uncertainties: Audit outcomes measure a specific early stage of hiring and do not alone identify all mechanisms of labour-market inequality.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Dynamic-panel GMM methods gave applied economists durable tools for treating persistence, unobserved heterogeneity, and endogeneity in panel data.
assessment.attribution: Arellano, Blundell, and Bond are the clear central contributors to the named framework.
assessment.maturity: The methods are longstanding, broadly used, and accompanied by a large literature on their strengths and limitations.
uncertainties: Routine application can be fragile when instruments proliferate or assumptions are weak.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Partial identification changed the discipline's treatment of what data can credibly establish when point-identifying assumptions are unavailable.
assessment.attribution: Manski is the decisive intellectual source of the core framework.
assessment.maturity: The approach is mature, theoretically well developed, and increasingly consequential in applied work.
uncertainties: Its practical influence is dispersed across many applications rather than concentrated in one empirical breakthrough.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The modern monopsony framework fundamentally revised how economists understand wage setting, employer power, and labour-market policy.
assessment.attribution: Manning provides the most distinct and foundational contribution to the modern revival of monopsony analysis.
assessment.maturity: The ideas have been widely taken up in empirical labour research and policy discussion.
uncertainties: The appropriate empirical interpretation of observed wage-setting power varies substantially across settings.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Collective household models replaced the unitary-family benchmark with a tractable framework for allocation, bargaining, and distribution within families.
assessment.attribution: Chiappori and Lundberg are central figures in the theoretical and empirical development of the collective approach.
assessment.maturity: The framework has generated a large mature literature in family, labour, and development economics.
uncertainties: Empirical identification of intrahousehold bargaining and preferences often relies on demanding assumptions.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Research on fetal and early-life conditions established that health shocks and environments can have persistent consequences for human capital and later outcomes.
assessment.attribution: Currie and Almond are especially central to the empirical demonstration and diffusion of this research program.
assessment.maturity: A broad body of quasi-experimental evidence now supports the importance of early-life conditions.
uncertainties: Effect sizes and mechanisms vary by setting, and causal extrapolation to interventions requires care.
